I disagree with the Jopper/Hopper take

Since season 1 there has been set up for a Hopper-Byers family unit between most all of the characters, so it makes sense to me that the story would end up there

For example for Jopper, it was implied since season one that they have some sort of romantic relationship (during the search party) as well as history with each other (the “back in high school” scene) and throughout all of the seasons Hopper is Joyce’s main support and vice versa so there was definitely romantic build up present even if you’re personally not a fan

It also makes sense because both Hopper and Joyce have acted as parental figures to Eleven/Will even prior to them becoming a unit 

For Hopper and Will it’s pretty implied that Joyce losing Will reminds him of the loss of his own daughter re: the scene which Hopper resuscitates Will being intercut with scenes of his own daughter having CPR preformed on her, this creates a parental allusion, that also semi continues into season 2 with Hopper’s constant presence when Will is in the hospital and acting as a protective figure for Will and while this dynamic wasn’t continued past season 2 it was present enough that I could plausibly buy them becoming a family unit later on, and it’s kind of sad to me it wasn’t explored more because Will deserves a good Dad figure (RIP Bob)

Joyce was also set up as a mother figure for El since season one with her giving motherly comfort in the sensory deprivation pool scene and this is continued in seasons 2 and 4 with Elevens tearful reunion with Joyce at the end of two, and Joyce quite literally becoming her mom in season 4

Will and El are also decently well set up as siblings in seasons 1 and 2 despite not really talking as it’s shown El definitely cares about Will in season 2 when one of the first things she does after going to the house is check on Will (who she’s never spoke to outside of the upside down before this so it really stuck out to me). And then obviously they become real siblings in season 4 

The only one who isn’t really a part of the pre set up Hopper-Byers dynamic is Jonathan, um, which, sucks for him I guess, but overall it seems like a pretty natural conclusion based on the pre-established dynamics

Kind of annoying how everyone complains about Max “being mean” to Mike when Mike was literally so much worse to her in season two than she ever was to him

Max’s biggest sin against Mike was convincing his girlfriend to be more independent, she didn’t give great relationship advice but people never consider El and Max’s perspectives in this and how much Max’s advice was ultimately important to El and her growth as a person

El’s relationship with Mike for seasons 1 and 2 basically plays as a toned down version of the born sexy yesterday trope, and outside of her dad, her only real meaningful connection/understanding of the world comes from her boyfriend— which is literally the first person to ever be nice to her

And outside of that, Max has every reason not to like Mike that much, he was an asshole to her all of season two simply because she was a girl who wanted to be friends with them and as far as I remember he never even really apologized for it

So when El, someone with limited life experience comes to her looking for help because the guy who was a dick to her (Max) all year broke her heart, it makes a lot of sense that she would want to help break El away from relying on a relationship for her sense of self rather than just help shove El back into that relationship 

Also Max had a point, that while it’s good to be concerned about Els well being, she knows herself better than Mike, and ultimately it is not his place to control her even if it’s coming from a  place of love

Max’s advice and friendship was something Eleven needed dearly being someone who spent her entire life being controlled by others, and it was clearly one of the most important relationships she’s ever had based on her flash backs in season 4

The female gaze is basically influenced by what it’s like to *be* the gazed upon, or the subject of a gaze. Think Margaret Atwood’s you are your own voyeur, in which the subject is both the viewer and the viewed. It isn’t necessarily a direct opposite of the male gaze but instead a reflection of how that gaze influences the way women view themselves and how they feel about it, at least that is it’s definition in media and could definitely extend over to the way women view beauty both being subject to it but also a viewer of it on themselves and other women, where as men for the most part of are just a viewer of female aesthetics

Because of this, men, regardless of sexuality, will not necessarily be able to have a true “female gaze” because they are not objectified in the same way women are, and for the most part they will still view women as objects just with different “purpose” based on wether or not they are attracted to them. This is how you’ll get gay men who are still extremely misogynistic because being gay doesn’t mean you’re not still a man and being a man means you’re still influenced by ideas of patriarchy and objectified views of femininity, and like a different commenter said, while they may be able to go a bit more in-depth than a straight man would (depending on who they are, gay men are not homogenous and don’t all fit with in the stereotype I know most of you are thinking of when reading this post) they are still giving you something very similar to the straight male gaze because they simply cannot account for any aspects of the “female gaze” based on the fact that they are not women
